svg.text: In The Year 2000! cryptex: assembly and lock
Part outlines match the cut sheets. Build each sub-assembly apart, then put them together. Rings, washers and core stay loose. Not cutting templates.
Part IDs (the letter is the sub-assembly, the number, R (ring) or C (collar) is the layer from the bottom)
A1 x1: center of the floor, under the core
A2R x1: glued face, in the rim
A2C x1: glued face, in the collar
A3R x1: glued face, in the rim
A3C x1: glued face, in the collar
A4R x1: glued face, in the rim
A4C x1: glued face, in the collar
A5R x1: glued face, in the rim
A5C x1: glued face, in the collar
E1 x1: glued face, in the rim
(E2) x1: unmarked: bare on top
D1 x1: glued face, in the rim
D2 x1: under the next ring up
C1 x1: glued face, in the rim
C2 x1: under the next ring up
B1 x1: glued face, in the rim
B2 x1: under the next ring up
G1 x2: glued face, in the washer
G2 x2: glued face, in the washer
G3 x2: glued face, in the washer
G4 x2: glued face, in the washer
(CORE0) x1: unmarked: too narrow for letters
(CORER) x2: unmarked: too narrow for letters
(COREC) x9: unmarked: too narrow for letters
(HEAD) x1: unmarked: bare on top
(LID) x1: unmarked: bare on top
(LIDP) x2: unmarked: too narrow for letters
An ID is engraved only on a face that ends up covered, so it never shows. Unmarked parts are listed in (brackets): the core slices and the plugs are
too narrow, the digit slice of ring 1, the head and the lid are bare on top.

g.text: Stack A: the base
A1
A2R
A2C
Glue the base stack from the bottom: A1, then A2R and A2C, up
to A5R and A5C. Keep the ridge slots of A2C to A5C lined up,
on the marker side (right).
It is the slowest to cure and carries the rest, so it goes
first, under a weight. Stand the dry core F in the slots as a
pin to line the collars up.
Sub-assembly A is one solid: a floor, a hollow ring and a
collar round the ridge slot.
Stacks B, C, D, E: the four rings
B1
B2
E1
E2
Glue ring 4 (stack B): the top slice B2 with the digits over
the plain slice B1, outer edges flush. Keep glue off the
socket. Sub-assembly B is one solid: ring 4, a rim under the
digit slice.
Glue ring 3 (stack C): the top slice C2 with the digits over
the plain slice C1, outer edges flush. Keep glue off the
socket. Sub-assembly C is one solid: ring 3, a rim under the
digit slice.
Glue ring 2 (stack D): the top slice D2 with the digits over
the plain slice D1, outer edges flush. Keep glue off the
socket. Sub-assembly D is one solid: ring 2, a rim under the
digit slice.
Glue ring 1 (stack E): the top slice E2 with the digits over
the plain slice E1, outer edges flush. Keep glue off the
socket. Sub-assembly E is one solid: ring 1, a rim under the
digit slice.
A ring must turn freely on the core, so it is glued to nothing
else. Rings are made apart and cure at the same time.
Stack F: the core
CORE0
CORER
COREC
Glue the 12 core slices in a stack: the closed one (CORE0) at
the bottom, two with the ridge (CORER, ridges lined up), then
nine round ones (COREC). No glue in the hole.
It is the one part that must stay straight and slide out of
the rings, so it is glued as a stack on a rolled tube that
lines up the holes.
Sub-assembly F is one solid: a tube closed at the bottom, a
ridge near it.
G1 to G4: the washer pairs
G1
G2
Glue the two washers G1 flat together, notches lined up (6
mm). Keep glue out of the bore and the notch. Sub-assembly G1
is one solid washer for ring 1.
Glue the two washers G2 flat together, notches lined up (6
mm). Keep glue out of the bore and the notch. Sub-assembly G2
is one solid washer for ring 2.
Glue the two washers G3 flat together, notches lined up (6
mm). Keep glue out of the bore and the notch. Sub-assembly G3
is one solid washer for ring 3.
Glue the two washers G4 flat together, notches lined up (6
mm). Keep glue out of the bore and the notch. Sub-assembly G4
is one solid washer for ring 4.
Two washers make a part as thick as its ring, and the pair
stays loose so it can be lifted out and turned.
H the head and I the lid
HEAD
LID
LIDP
The head H is one slice. It has no sub-assembly.
The head H is ready.
Only the head is glued on the core, and it goes on last, above
the rings, so the rings stay on.
Glue the two plugs under the lid, one on the other.
Sub-assembly I is one solid: the lid with its plug.
The plugs press into the core and hold the lid, so they are
glued together first.

svg.text: Final assembly: put the finished sub-assemblies together
1. Stand core F in base stack A, its ridge to the marker. Do
not glue it.
2. Slide ring 4 (stack B) down over the core, digits up. It
must turn freely.
3. Drop washer pair G4 into the socket of ring 4, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
4. Slide ring 3 (stack C) down over the core, digits up. It
must turn freely.
5. Drop washer pair G3 into the socket of ring 3, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
6. Slide ring 2 (stack D) down over the core, digits up. It
must turn freely.
7. Drop washer pair G2 into the socket of ring 2, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
8. Slide ring 1 (stack E) down over the core, digits up. It
must turn freely.
9. Drop washer pair G1 into the socket of ring 1, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
10. Glue head H on the top of the core, over ring 1. Keep glue
off the rings.
11. Roll a note and slip it in the core; press lid I in.
Set your own code
1. To set your own code, dial 2 0 0 0 and pull the core F,
with its head H and lid I, straight up and out.
2. Lift ring 1 (stack E) off and set it aside. The washer pair
G1 stays loose.
3. Lift the washer pair G1 out of its socket.
4. Turn G1 so its notch lies under the digit you want. One
digit is 36 degrees: three digits moves the first digit from 2
to 5.
5. Drop G1 back in its socket.
6. Put ring 1 (stack E) back on, then dial it to the new
digit.
7. Push the core F back in. Do the same for D and G2, C and
G3, B and G4. Read the code from ring 1 out along the marker.

g.text: The lock: the ridge and a washer's notch (to scale)
Red: the core's ridge, at the marker. The washer is a ring's inner part.
Notch at the marker: the ridge passes
One digit off: the washer stops it
Setting and changing the combination
Seat each washer so its notch lies under the ring's digit you want.
Ring 1 (the smallest, on top) is the first digit and ring 4 the last,
read outward along the marker. It is set to 2000: ring 1 at 2, the rest at 0.
Each washer can sit ten ways, one per digit: 10,000 combinations.
The ridge is 4 mm wide, the notch 7 mm: a ring only has to be near its digit
(about 5 degrees), not exact. There are no detents, so look at the marker.

svg.text: Stack height 36 mm: four base layers (12), four rings of two slices (24). The core is 12 slices; the head sits on top.
